figure: Board-level additions from the kit layout sheet (not in any article figure)

parts.notes: 2 x 32 way at 0.1 in, at the top of the board between the memory and the tape interface. No article prints its pinout, so this one is ours: the system bus (A0-A15 straight from the Z80, D0-D7 on the buffered side of IC9-12, the buffered RD/WR/MREQ and the Z80's own IORQ, M1, RFSH, HALT, WAIT/BUSRQ, BUSAK, INT, NMI and RESET), the 2 MHz clock, MEM_MREQ_N (the IC17 side of LK3, which the Fig. 7 memory expansion drives once LK3 is removed), the eleven unused port selects from IC2 (OUT 00, 80, 40, C0, A0, E0) and IC3 (IN 04, 02, 06, 05, 07), and the supply rails. Odd pins are the row nearer the middle of the board. Pins 1 and 3 are left unconnected: the track from IC2 to the tape latch passes too close to them for a supply pad's clearance. The October 1980 floppy-disc controller needs exactly these: IC2 pin 10 (OUT A0) and IC3 pin 10 (IN 05) with A3, A4, D0-D7, the 2 MHz clock and INT.
Fig. 8 brings out Video, Sync and Sync-bar; the kit sheet has VIDEO and SYNC pads at the right-hand edge
